newsitem.title: USA: Democratic Congress would worry Wall St - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Democratic Congress would worry Wall St - analyst.

text.p: A return to power by Democrats in the November congressional elections could spark currency pressure, weakness in bonds and uncertainty for stocks, said Prudential Securities chief investment strategist Greg A. Smith.
Speaking at a news conference on Tuesday, Smith said he believed the chances of the Democrats staging a comeback were about 40 percent.

"The fear would be that (Democrats) would at least propose legislation either to punish business or make business pay for the agenda of things they would like to accomplish which would hurt profits," he said.

He said that any surprise, particularly a changeover in the House of Representatives, would be viewed as a disruption. Many on Wall Street have said they preferred to see power divided between Democrats and Republicans in Washington.

"It wouldn't surprise me if we saw some currency pressure and if we then saw the bond market worrying about weak currency causing inflation," Smith said. "And there would be the risk of spending that never gets paid for."
The Republicans swept into Congress in Midterm elections in 1994.
